rounded_feedback_no_fixed_point.derivation: A finite fixed point cannot be s<=0 (RHS>=1), s>=1 (RHS<=0.5), s<=0.5 (RHS>=0.75), or s>=0.75 (RHS<=0.625). Thus 0.5<s<0.75. Multiplication by -0.5 is exact here. 1-s/2 belongs to (0.625,0.75), whose binary64 spacing is 2^-53; final RN error <=2^-54. Hence |s-2/3|<=1/(3*2^53). The lower neighboring float L=0x1.5555555555555p-1 is exactly 1/(3*2^53) below 2/3, while U is 2/(3*2^53) above it, and all other floats are farther away. Only L is a possible fixed point. For L, 1-L/2 is the exact midpoint (L+U)/2; U has even significand, so RN gives U != L. Therefore no finite binary64 fixed point exists. The U->L computation is an additional 2-cycle illustration, not the global exclusion proof.
